Incident.name: INC-1001
Incident.title: notifications consumer lag on user-events
Incident.summary: notifications fell 61,000 messages behind on topic user-events after PR #1116 (switch consumer to manual batch commit). Nothing customer facing failed, downstream work was delayed by ~0 min.

Incident.name: INC-1002
Incident.title: user-profile overloaded by retries from ads
Incident.summary: user-profile p99 jumped to 900ms and ads started returning 5xx. PR #1127 raised retries.user-profile on ads from 1 to 5; every slow call was retried and user-profile load went up ~5x.
Incident.fix: set retries.user-profile back to 1 and added jittered backoff

Incident.name: INC-1003
Incident.title: catalog-db overloaded, search cache disabled
Incident.summary: catalog-db p99 hit 410ms and search, frontend started returning 5xx after PR #1130 set cache_enabled=false on search (debugging stale results); every read went to the database.

Incident.name: INC-1004
Incident.title: inventory overloaded by retries from search
Incident.summary: inventory p99 jumped to 1600ms and search, frontend started returning 5xx. PR #1136 raised retries.inventory on search from 1 to 5; every slow call was retried and inventory load went up ~5x.
Incident.fix: set retries.inventory back to 1 and added jittered backoff

Incident.name: INC-1005
Incident.title: frontend TLS errors to image-resizer
Incident.summary: frontend failed TLS handshakes to image-resizer (cert expired at 00:00 UTC). image-resizer itself was healthy, nothing was deployed.
Incident.fix: rotated the image-resizer cert and added an expiry alert

Incident.name: INC-1006
Incident.title: auth 5xx after github.com/golang-jwt/jwt upgrade
Incident.summary: auth started returning 5xx right after PR #1153 bumped github.com/golang-jwt/jwt v4.5.0 -> v5.2.1 and frontend started returning 5xx: v5 validates the nbf claim strictly and our mobile tokens have clock skew.

Incident.name: INC-1007
Incident.title: catalog-db overloaded, reviews cache disabled
Incident.summary: catalog-db p99 hit 380ms and reviews started returning 5xx after PR #1167 set cache_enabled=false on reviews (cache showing deleted reviews); every read went to the database.

Incident.name: INC-1008
Incident.title: analytics consumer lag on inventory-events
Incident.summary: analytics fell 520,000 messages behind on topic inventory-events during the evening order peak. Nothing customer facing failed, downstream work was delayed by ~4 min.
Incident.fix: scaled the consumer group from 3 to 8 replicas

Incident.name: INC-1009
Incident.title: email overloaded by retries from notifications
Incident.summary: email p99 jumped to 4200ms and notifications started returning 5xx. PR #1171 raised retries.email on notifications from 2 to 6; every slow call was retried and email load went up ~6x.
Incident.fix: set retries.email back to 2 and added jittered backoff

Incident.name: INC-1010
Incident.title: user-profile 5xx after google.golang.org/protobuf upgrade
Incident.summary: user-profile started returning 5xx right after PR #1172 bumped google.golang.org/protobuf v1.33.0 -> v1.34.0 and ads started returning 5xx: unknown enum values now fail to unmarshal, profiles with the new tier field 500.

Incident.name: INC-1011
Incident.title: reviews TLS errors to catalog-db
Incident.summary: reviews failed TLS handshakes to catalog-db (cert expired at 00:00 UTC). catalog-db itself was healthy, nothing was deployed.
Incident.fix: rotated the catalog-db cert and added an expiry alert

Incident.name: INC-1012
Incident.title: accounting consumer lag on orders
Incident.summary: accounting fell 184,000 messages behind on topic orders during the evening order peak. Nothing customer facing failed, downstream work was delayed by ~1 min.
Incident.fix: scaled the consumer group from 3 to 8 replicas

Incident.name: INC-1013
Incident.title: user-profile latency spike, orders-db pool exhausted
Incident.summary: user-profile p99 went to 1900ms and ads, frontend started returning 5xx. The orders-db connection pool was exhausted after PR #1181 lowered pool.orders-db from 25 to 10; peak concurrency is ~20.

Incident.name: INC-1014
Incident.title: user-profile 5xx after new_profile_api rollout
Incident.summary: user-profile returned 5xx for ~45% of requests and ads started returning 5xx once PR #1190 flipped new_profile_api to true for everyone (rollout to 100%).

Incident.name: INC-1015
Incident.title: accounting latency spike, ledger-db pool exhausted
Incident.summary: accounting p99 went to 3100ms. The ledger-db connection pool was exhausted after PR #1189 lowered pool.ledger-db from 20 to 8; peak concurrency is ~16.

Incident.name: INC-1016
Incident.title: search 5xx after elasticsearch-java upgrade
Incident.summary: search started returning 5xx right after PR #1192 bumped elasticsearch-java 8.13.4 -> 9.0.1 and frontend started returning 5xx: the 9.x client rejects our index mapping so every query 500s.

Incident.name: INC-1017
Incident.title: sessions overloaded by retries from auth
Incident.summary: sessions p99 jumped to 650ms and auth, frontend started returning 5xx. PR #1200 raised retries.sessions on auth from 1 to 4; every slow call was retried and sessions load went up ~4x.
Incident.fix: set retries.sessions back to 1 and added jittered backoff

Incident.name: INC-1018
Incident.title: auth TLS errors to sessions
Incident.summary: auth failed TLS handshakes to sessions (cert expired at 00:00 UTC) and frontend started returning 5xx. sessions itself was healthy, nothing was deployed.
Incident.fix: rotated the sessions cert and added an expiry alert

Incident.name: INC-1019
Incident.title: inventory latency spike, inventory-db pool exhausted
Incident.summary: inventory p99 went to 2400ms and search started returning 5xx. The inventory-db connection pool was exhausted after PR #1208 lowered pool.inventory-db from 40 to 15; peak concurrency is ~30.

Incident.name: INC-1020
Incident.title: fraud-detection latency spike, orders-db pool exhausted
Incident.summary: fraud-detection p99 went to 2700ms. The orders-db connection pool was exhausted after PR #1215 lowered pool.orders-db from 16 to 6; peak concurrency is ~12.

FailurePattern.name: kafka_lag
FailurePattern.description: A consumer group falls behind its topic; downstream effects (ledger, emails) are delayed.

FailurePattern.name: retry_storm
FailurePattern.description: Aggressive retries against a slow dependency multiply its load until it falls over.

FailurePattern.name: flag_misconfig
FailurePattern.description: A feature flag flipped in production changes load or behaviour in an unexpected way.

FailurePattern.name: cert_expiry
FailurePattern.description: An expired TLS certificate breaks handshakes; the callee is healthy but unreachable.

FailurePattern.name: bad_dependency_bump
FailurePattern.description: A library upgrade changes behaviour and breaks the service that shipped it.

FailurePattern.name: db_pool_exhaustion
FailurePattern.description: Connection pool smaller than the service's peak concurrency; requests queue for a connection, latency climbs and callers time out.

Lesson.name: L-1001
Lesson.text: Autoscale notifications on partition lag and alert at 10k. In INC-1001 it fell 61,000 messages behind on user-events.

Lesson.name: L-1008
Lesson.text: Autoscale analytics on partition lag and alert at 10k. In INC-1008 it fell 520,000 messages behind on inventory-events.

Lesson.name: L-1012
Lesson.text: Autoscale accounting on partition lag and alert at 10k. In INC-1012 it fell 184,000 messages behind on orders.

Lesson.name: L-1002
Lesson.text: Cap retries at 2 with jittered backoff. In INC-1002, ads raised retries.user-profile 1->5 and the retries multiplied load on an already slow user-profile.

Lesson.name: L-1004

Lesson.name: L-1017

Lesson.name: L-1003

Lesson.name: L-1005
Lesson.text: Alert 14 days before a cert expires and rotate with cert-manager. In INC-1005 the image-resizer cert expired; frontend saw TLS errors while image-resizer was healthy.

Lesson.name: L-1011

Lesson.name: L-1010
Lesson.text: Canary major dependency bumps and read the changelog. In INC-1010, google.golang.org/protobuf v1.33.0->v1.34.0 in user-profile: unknown enum values now fail to unmarshal, profiles with the new tier field 500.

Decision.name: Consumers autoscale on partition lag
Decision.title: Consumers autoscale on partition lag
Decision.text: Consumer groups scale on lag via KEDA; alert when lag > 10k messages for 5 minutes.

Decision.name: Max 2 retries with jittered backoff
Decision.title: Max 2 retries with jittered backoff
Decision.text: Sync calls retry at most twice, with exponential backoff and jitter. Anything more needs a retry budget on the callee side.

Decision.name: Cache flags are reviewed like config
Decision.title: Cache flags are reviewed like config
Decision.text: Flags that change load (caches, new code paths) need a load check and a second reviewer.

Decision.name: Alert 14 days before any cert expires
Decision.title: Alert 14 days before any cert expires
Decision.text: All internal certs are issued by cert-manager with 30-day rotation and an expiry alert at 14 days.

Decision.name: Major dependency bumps ship behind a canary
Decision.title: Major dependency bumps ship behind a canary
Decision.text: Major-version bumps are canaried on 5% of traffic for 30 minutes before full rollout.

Decision.name: DB pools stay at or above peak concurrency
Decision.title: DB pools stay at or above peak concurrency
Decision.text: Every service sizes its DB pool to at least its measured peak concurrency. Pool changes go through the platform team.

Detector.name: D-1017 retries_without_backoff
Detector.cypher:
UNWIND $changes AS ch
MATCH path = (k:ConfigKey {service: ch.service, key: ch.key})-[:CONFIGURES]->(a:Service)
WHERE k.kind = 'retries'
WITH ch, k, a, path
WHERE toFloat(toString(ch.new)) > $max_retries
  AND (ch.old IS NULL OR toFloat(toString(ch.new)) > toFloat(toString(ch.old)))
OPTIONAL MATCH target = (k)-[:TARGETS]->(b:Service)
RETURN ch.service AS service, ch.key AS key, ch.new AS proposed, null AS safe_min,
       a.name AS caller, b.name AS callee, null AS p99, ch.sha AS sha, path, target

Detector.name: D-1007 flag_disables_cache
Detector.cypher:
UNWIND $changes AS ch
MATCH path = (k:ConfigKey {service: ch.service, key: ch.key})-[:CONFIGURES]->(a:Service)
WHERE k.kind = 'flag' AND toLower(k.key) CONTAINS 'cache'
  AND toLower(toString(ch.new)) IN ['false', '0', '0.000000', 'off', 'disabled']
OPTIONAL MATCH target = (k)-[:TARGETS]->(b:Service)
RETURN ch.service AS service, ch.key AS key, ch.new AS proposed, null AS safe_min,
       a.name AS caller, b.name AS callee, null AS p99, ch.sha AS sha, path, target

Detector.name: D-1020 pool_below_concurrency
Detector.cypher:
UNWIND $changes AS ch
MATCH path = (k:ConfigKey {service: ch.service, key: ch.key})-[:CONFIGURES]->(a:Service)
WHERE k.kind = 'pool' AND a.peak_concurrency IS NOT NULL
WITH ch, k, a, path
WHERE toFloat(toString(ch.new)) < a.peak_concurrency * $factor
OPTIONAL MATCH target = (k)-[:TARGETS]->(b:Service)
RETURN ch.service AS service, ch.key AS key, ch.new AS proposed,
       toInteger(ceil(a.peak_concurrency * $factor)) AS safe_min,
       a.name AS caller, b.name AS callee, null AS p99, ch.sha AS sha, path, target

Runbook.name: Payment latency
Runbook.title: Payment latency
Runbook.text:
Owner: payments team (#payments-oncall).
If checkout throws 5xx and payment dashboards look fine, check the checkout->payment timeout first.
Current setting: timeouts_ms.payment = 800ms. payment p99 is ~450ms on a normal day, higher during sales. Dont go below ~700ms without a load test.
Payment itself rarely fails, usually its the caller giving up too early.

Runbook.name: Shipping quotes
Runbook.title: Shipping quotes
Runbook.text:
quote is slow by design (it calls the carrier APIs), p99 ~300ms.
shipping->quote timeout is 600ms (raised from 500 after the carrier latency bump).
If quotes fail check the carrier status page before touching config.

Runbook.name: Checkout on-call
Runbook.title: Checkout on-call
Runbook.text:
Checkout on-call cheat sheet.
1. Check frontend + checkout 5xx in grafana.
2. Timeouts: shipping 1200ms, payment 800ms, cart/currency 300ms.
3. Roll back the last deploy if it is < 30 min old, ask questions later.

Runbook.name: DB pool exhaustion
Runbook.title: DB pool exhaustion
Runbook.text:
Symptom: p99 climbs on one service, DB itself looks idle.
Check pool wait time metric. Pool size must be >= peak concurrency (see the service README).
Fix: restore pool size, do NOT restart the db.

Runbook.name: Retry storms
Runbook.title: Retry storms
Runbook.text:
If a callee is slow and its callers are erroring, look at retry counts first.
We allow max 2 retries w/ jittered backoff. More than that = storm.
search->inventory retries: 1. auth->sessions retries: 1.

Runbook.name: Cert rotation
Runbook.title: Cert rotation
Runbook.text: Certs are issued by cert-manager. If you see handshake errors, run kubectl get certificates -A and check NotAfter. Expiry alert fires 14d before.

Runbook.name: Dependency upgrades
Runbook.title: Dependency upgrades
Runbook.text:
Minor/patch bumps from deps-bot can merge on green CI.
Major bumps: canary 5% for 30min, read the changelog, get a second reviewer.

Runbook.name: Feature flags
Runbook.title: Feature flags
Runbook.text:
Flags live in config/services.yaml under flags.*
cache_enabled should always be true in prod. new_profile_api is at 10% rollout.
Flip flags in the evening, not during the lunch peak.

Runbook.name: Kafka consumer lag
Runbook.title: Kafka consumer lag
Runbook.text:
Lag alert = consumer group behind its topic. Customer flows keep working, ledger/emails are delayed.
Scale the consumer group (KEDA) before restarting anything; restarts trigger a rebalance.
